claims.text: The site names no owner, author or organisation anywhere on the pages opened. Its footer gives only 'Email: Flux_liners@icloud.com', a 'Privacy Policy' link and 'Site by Blueqube' pointing at https://blueqube.org.uk . It carries no copyright notice and no licence statement of any kind on the FLUX 1988, TECH or SHOP pages.

The site is the host of two of the three primary documents in this thread: the Scott 1990 interview notes, under the link text 'SORENSEN 1990 INTERVIEW' with a Download button, and the McCandlish coroner's file, under the link text 'Coroner's report on Mark MaCandlish's death' pointing at a Google Drive item named 'C21-0324 McCandlish.pdf'.

The 3D reconstruction is the site operator's own work, built from secondary material and not from the original drawing. The page states: 'This is my 3D recreation of the craft they described. I rebuilt it from the ground up, using measurements from the original sketches and information provided by Mark in his talks and videos', and, for a second version, 'using measurements from the original sketches and information provided by Mark from online live streams and podcast apperences.'

The page states that the original McCandlish artwork could not be obtained: 'Fascinated by this story I tried to find an original copy of Mark's work to buy. Unfortunately, now that Mark has passed on it's impossible to get hold of. I imagine that Steven Greer may have it or at least a copy.'
The renders are sold. The shop lists three products, 'ARV_2009', 'Fluxliner full colour' and 'Fluxliner Illustrated', at 30.00 each, with no licence terms stated.

The site's own stated theory of how the craft works is not McCandlish's and is not sourced to him. Its TECH page lists 'Magnetohydrodynamics', 'Quasicrystals', 'Einstein-Rosen bridge theory', 'The Hutchinson effect' and 'Levels of consciousness' among 'Our current lines of thinking', and leans on Bob Greenyer of the Martin Fleischmann Memorial Project, a Lockheed Martin matterwave patent, Thomas Bearden and Malcolm Bendall. A reader who takes the site as a source on the 1990 account is reading two different things bound together.

desc: The custody node for two of the three primary documents in this thread, in the same role the board already gives the-black-vault, and with two differences the node has to say out loud. Its owner is unnamed: no author, no organisation and no copyright or licence statement appears anywhere on the pages opened, only an icloud.com address and a credit to a site builder. And it sells what it publishes. Its 3D reconstruction is the site operator's own work, built from the 2001 testimony and from McCandlish's later talks and podcast appearances rather than from the original drawing, which the page says could not be obtained; prints of that reconstruction are on sale at 30.00 each with no licence terms stated. Its TECH page then sets out a theory of operation that is not McCandlish's and is sourced to nobody in this thread. A reader who takes the site as a source on the 1990 account is reading two different things bound together.

unverified: The site's unsigned RESEARCH page gives McCandlish's life dates as '(1957 - 2021)' and calls him 'an American aerospace illustrator, conceptual artist, and researcher'. It cites no source and the birth year cannot be reconciled with the coroner's record. The board carries no birth year for him.

Any licence under which the 3D reconstruction could be reused. The site carries no licence statement at all and sells prints, so the reconstruction must be treated as somebody else's copyrighted work. No 'break apart' animation with a stated licence was opened.
